schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of WHO came through it. `write(path, content, verb=, why=)` writes atomically (temp + replace, the existing mode preserved) and, when the path is a record of truth by `jurisdiction.json`, appends a hash-chained entry to `<root>/.artifact-journal.jsonl` carrying the sha256 before and after, the verb, the why, the caller's CLASS read from the kernel's cgroup ancestry for the process (gate = a `cairn-*.service` unit; cc = the `superclaude-<pid>.scope` the launcher puts every session in; akien = a desktop-app or login-session scope; else unknown), the raw cgroup and unit, the process ancestry, and the top six stack frames as testimony. `check_staged(root)` is the pre-commit question: every staged record's blob must hash to the journal's last `sha_after` for that path (a deletion's last entry must say absent; a never-journaled record is refused as such), the chain replays clean, and the journal is staged alongside. `genesis(root)` journals every standing record once. `park_hand_edit(path, why)` restores a record edited around the door to its journaled bytes and parks the proposed bytes for Akien; `approve(id, words)` journals verb=hand-edit with his words and REFUSES a caller whose measured class is not akien; `refuse(id, words)` discards. `set_diagnostic_roots` / `CAIRN_ARTIFACT_ROOTS` hand the door a scratch world. Two hooks ride it: the tracked `hooks/pre-commit` (installed into CairnCommons by `cairn artifact install-hook`) and the first, BLOCKING step of the tester's `cairn/devices/tester/hooks/pre-commit`; `bin/cmd/artifactgate` is the PreToolUse gate that refuses an Edit/Write/Bash aimed at a record before the edit is made.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: ticket 481221f45884 stood at [PROVED] with no crossing in the harbor journal — its cursor had been moved by hand in commit 42e3db0 on 2026-09-10, and nothing in the system could say so until a reader compared two records by eye. 'Records go through their door' was a memory and a paragraph; a census on 2026-09-13 found 145 code sites in 69 files writing record paths with write_text. Akien, 2026-09-13: 'we have to build a machine that you must use to update .artifacts and the job of the machine will be in part to assure that a hand edits only happen with an explicit from me to allow that ... the machine does an introspective call stack check and records who called it. the gates can trigger the mechanism (normal flow), command line (me), and you.' WHO IS KERNEL TRUTH, WHY IS TESTIMONY: a caller cannot forge its cgroup from inside its own process, and the ancestry walk means a scope CC spawns to look like a hand at a terminal still has the claude process — in its superclaude scope — as an ancestor (measured 2026-09-13: `systemd-run --user --scope` moves a child but does not reparent it). The call stack he asked for rides beside it as provenance and never decides trust, because a stack is a claim the caller makes. WHY THE JOURNAL LIVES IN THE REPO: the commit is the one moment every change to a record passes, and after it the hand edit IS the record — so the check has to run there, against a journal that travels with the records it describes. WHY A HAND EDIT IS PARKED AND NOT FORBIDDEN: his design — a hand edit needs an explicit approval from him through the existing inspection process — and `cairn ruling open` needs his verbatim words, so the park is what waits for them, and the approval is itself measured rather than taken from a packet. WHY A TOOL (Law 6): the journal is the record repo's state, owned by whoever owns that repo's records; every per-class door (validation store, history append, trouble device, ruling intake, skill doors, set_phase) keeps its own verb and calls this to do the write.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.artifact import artifact as door; door.write(path, text, verb='cast', why='...')`. CLI: `cairn artifact write|remove|genesis|check|verify|caller|locate|hand-edit|parked|approve|refuse|install-hook`. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_artifact_door.py` and `python3 bin/proofs/test_artifact_gate.py`. The PreToolUse face: `cairn artifactgate` (bin/cmd/artifactgate, wired in .claude/settings.json on Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Bash; reads the tool call on stdin, exit 2 refuses and names `cairn artifact hand-edit`). The jurisdiction is `cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json` — one spelling, read by the door, the hook and the gate.
entry: Written 2026-09-13 under ticket 30531f6e1c5d, pre-approved through PROVED by Akien ('approved thru PROVED RULED BLESSED FROM ON HIGH'). Patterns cited, not grafted: the atomic temp+replace is the shape validation_store and transitions already used; the caller read composes cairn.tools.cgroup (the corpus's one reader of /proc/<pid>/cgroup) and reads /proc/<pid>/stat for the parent, as sail_record already does; the co-occurrence gate is deletegate's trade taken again with its eyes open; the tracked hook + install + byte-identical verify is the tester's host-seam recipe.
state_and_history: The journal (`.artifact-journal.jsonl` at each record root) is the RECORD REPO'S state, not this tool's — it berths beside the records it describes and is committed with them, because a journal that did not travel with the records could not answer the commit question in a fresh clone. Parked hand edits berth under the operator's holder at ~/.cairn/devices/operator/0/tools/artifact/parked/ (ruling 2026-08-14-tools-and-machines-remember-under-their-holder). No state.json or history.json beside this charter.
filed_edges: (a) `git commit --no-verify` and a session with hooks off walk around both checks. The check is policy at the commit; the physics is a second unix user owning the record roots with this door the only path through the sudo relay — the ticket's owed_physics, named and not paid here. OPEN.

(b) THE ONE MEASURED ESCAPE FROM THE CALLER READ: a scope CC spawns AND a daemonising double-fork inside it (reparenting to systemd) reads as akien. Two deliberate steps; the same owed physics closes it. Measured 2026-09-13 in proofs/test_artifact_door.py (the forged scope alone still reads cc).

(c) THE CLASSIFIER IS A REGEX OVER ONE HOST'S UNIT NAMES ON ONE DAY. A new launcher, a renamed unit or a session started some way nobody measured reads as unknown — journaled, and the probe `probes/callers_are_known.py` fires on the first one so the regex is taught before the journal fills.

(d) 145 SITES STILL WRITE RECORD PATHS AROUND THE DOOR (census 2026-09-13). Seven doors are wired (validation store, projector, trouble device, ruling intake, saveslate door, idea door, set_phase); the rest are the rename ticket's worklist, and until then each such write reds at the commit question, which is the design — a red that names its fix, not a silent pass.

(e) THE JOURNAL GROWS WITHOUT BOUND and `_append` re-reads it to find the tail (893 + 399 entries at genesis, ~1.4 MB). Measured 4.6 s for the 893-entry genesis; ordinary writes are one append. A rotation would need a chain anchor — not built until measured to matter (Law 8).

(f) A GENESIS ENTRY NAMES NO REAL WHO: every record that predates the door is journaled once with the genesis verb and the caller that ran genesis (cc, 2026-09-13). The who of those 1,292 records is the commit author in git, and the journal does not pretend otherwise.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_artifact_door.py (three real callers measured, the door over a scratch world, the commit question, the hand-edit round trip, the chain, genesis, the hook blocking in a scratch clone) and bin/proofs/test_artifact_gate.py under the tester. Commit gate — the check itself, running in both repos' pre-commit. Build gate — the PreToolUse artifactgate. Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a record of truth in a jurisdiction root reaches a commit with bytes the journal's last entry does not hash to, and the pre-commit check let it pass; (2) a journal entry's caller class disagrees with the cgroup the kernel reports for that process — or reads unknown for a gate, this session, or a hand at a terminal on this host; (3) an entry can be altered or removed without verify_chain naming it; (4) approve succeeds from a process whose measured class is not akien (the forged-scope tooth is the instrument); (5) a write outside the jurisdiction is journaled, or a write inside it is not; (6) the hook, the gate and the door disagree about what is a record — the jurisdiction is one file and a second spelling is the red. WRONG INTENT: if after 500 writes the journal names only cc — no gate ever wrote a record through it and Akien never approved a hand edit — the door measured one hand, and the who it was built to record was never in question.
proof: proofs/test_artifact_door.py — 61 teeth, GREEN 2026-09-13 (sealed under netns), one declared per falsifier clause (PROVES['30531f6e1c5d'] 1–5): gate/cc/akien measured over a transient cairn-*.service, this session's scope, a scope CC forged (reads cc by ancestry), and live processes in session-N.scope / app-*.scope; the CLI face agreeing with the in-process read; the door over a scratch world (journaled write, chained entries, no-op on same bytes, out-of-jurisdiction plain write, 0444 preserved, no-why and bad-verb refused); the writers (validation_store seal, projector append, transitions phase) each journaling with their verb; check_staged refusing a hand edit and a never-journaled record and passing a door write; park/approve(refused from cc)/refuse; a tampered entry named; genesis idempotent; remove and rename journaled; install-hook into a scratch clone blocking `git commit` of an unjournaled record and passing a journaled tree; the tester's hook refusing BEFORE its reseal ladder; the charter and probe beside the code; the live cairn journal verifying from genesis and the live CairnCommons journal untouched by the scratch world. bin/proofs/test_artifact_gate.py — the PreToolUse verdicts and the settings.json wiring on Write/Edit/MultiEdit/Bash.
owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Its users: validation_store, charter/projector, the trouble device, the ruling intake, the saveslate and idea doors, transitions.set_phase, the two pre-commit hooks, artifactgate. The journal is owned by the record repo; the parked edits by the operator. CC writes the code and proofs; Akien owns the design and is the only hand that approves a hand edit.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — the who is read from the kernel, never claimed)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — the commit check is the physics we have; the second unix user is the IOU)
Law 6 (a tool has users; the journal is the record repo's state)
Law 7 (a record of truth never collapses an error — a hand edit is parked, never written as truth, and a chain fault is named, never skipped)
Law 9 (red is the default — a write around the door reds at commit until it is parked and approved)
provenance: Born 2026-09-13 from the artifact-door design conversation (intent berth intent-20260913T162759-ed581acb3f53, sorted berth sorted-20260913T163219-5da2fd579a7b), ruled P0 and pre-approved through PROVED. The first thing built was the three-caller measurement, because the design rests on the kernel telling the three apart and nothing else was worth writing until it did.
learns: The journal is the substrate two follow-ons learn from: the `.artifact` rename (which collapses the jurisdiction to one extension) and the counting learning block over who-writes-what (the Friston free-energy idea — expected write rates per class and verb, surprise when they move). The door itself learns one thing: its classifier, taught by the probe each time an unknown appears.
how_it_learns: Through probes/callers_are_known.py: on the beat it counts journaled writes by caller class across both roots, fires to harbor_master carrying every unknown (root, path, cgroup), and retires once 500 writes across all three classes carry zero unknown and the hand-edit route has been exercised once. Each fire is one regex taught; the count is the evidence that the classifier covers the host.
